requirements.requirement: /srv/data set up to be recoverable through filesystem snapshots (persistent, snapshot-capable storage)
requirements.summary: A loop-backed btrfs image was created, formatted, a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data, and fstab entries added. Persistence was verified by unmounting and re-running 'mount -a', which correctly remounted both the top-level btrfs filesystem and the /srv/data subvolume (cmd-39d44759563b4470). This was independently reconfirmed after a full node reboot (cmd-c4d738d025464a08), showing the setup survives a real restart, not just a manual remount test.

requirements.requirement: Baseline application data present and a snapshot captured before modification
requirements.summary: Baseline files (settings.conf, app.log, records.txt) were created under /srv/data with recorded SHA-256 hashes, then a read-only btrfs snapshot 'data-snap-20260929-111016' was created of the subvolume at that point.

requirements.requirement: /srv/data modified after the snapshot was taken (to create a divergence to recover from)
requirements.summary: After the snapshot, settings.conf was edited, records.txt deleted, junk.txt added, and app.log appended. Resulting hashes differ from the pre-modification baseline, directly evidencing the divergence.

requirements.requirement: Exact restoration of /srv/data content to the earlier snapshot's state
requirements.summary: The live subvolume was deleted and recreated as a writable snapshot of the read-only snapshot. Post-restore file listing and SHA-256 hashes (cmd-a5c5df278fa54390) exactly match the original pre-modification baseline hashes captured in cmd-171533d92fe741bf: junk.txt is gone, records.txt is back, settings.conf and app.log content match. This is a direct before/after comparison, not just a final-state claim.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/mount state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 901ef286... with /srv/data mounted and hashes matching the restored baseline (cmd-def8dbd02a8a4d9a). A backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' was issued and acknowledged (cmd-4379bf8c20964660), followed by observed connection loss (cmd-0e39521862b24f96, cmd-4fa1109eb4194a89) and reconnection with a new boot_id 6dbf2779... and fresh uptime (cmd-738f7a94f1f74d0b). Post-reboot, the loop device, both fstab mounts, and btrfs subvolumes were confirmed intact with file hashes still matching baseline (cmd-c4d738d025464a08). This is cross-checked by the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity observations, which independently show the same boot_id transition (901ef286... to 6dbf2779...).

overall_summary: The executor set up /srv/data as a persistent, snapshot-capable btrfs subvolume, took a snapshot of baseline data, modified the directory, and restored it to the exact pre-modification content, verified via SHA-256 hashes before and after. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a clean pre/post boot-identity transition and confirmed post-reboot recovery of the mount and data, cross-checked against the fixed global snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: Evidence for filesystem-level recoverability relies on a single snapshot/modify/restore cycle rather than multiple snapshot generations; this is sufficient to satisfy the literal task contract but doesn't demonstrate handling of multiple retained snapshots.

Underlying storage is a loop-mounted image rather than a native block device, which is a reasonable implementation choice given the base ext4 root filesystem, but relies on 'nofail' fstab options whose failure-mode behavior was not separately tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: provisioning the loop-backed btrfs image and mount (cmd-f3f0c1a26e0f4d6b, cmd-0462653e318c41ba), fstab persistence and its verification via unmount/mount -a (cmd-5840583f730948ad, cmd-39d44759563b4470), baseline data creation and snapshot (cmd-171533d92fe741bf, cmd-5e53e4da63cf4e8c), the required modification (cmd-36a33e7acfa84ecc), the restore (cmd-5f0c2d0cc5204a9a), and the mandatory reboot (cmd-4379bf8c20964660). No unrelated or unrestored experimental mutations were found. The two 'failed' commands (cmd-0e39521862b24f96, cmd-4fa1109eb4194a89) are expected connectivity drops during the reboot, not troubleshooting mutations. Retained artifacts (/var/lib/srv-data-backing image, /mnt/srvdata-top mount point, fstab entries, btrfs subvolumes/snapshots) are all necessary infrastructure for the snapshot-recoverability requirement, not residue. The global lifecycle diff shows only the expected boot-identity/socket/tmp-dir changes from the reboot itself, with no failed services or unexplained package-state changes.
